newsitem.title: PERU: Peru growth prospects tied to "El Nino" - Fujimori.
newsitem.headline: Peru growth prospects tied to "El Nino" - Fujimori.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori said Thursday his country's short-term economic growth prospects would be linked to a destructive weather system that could form later this year.

"The success of the process of relaunching our economy, a relaunching currently underway, (is) conditioned to the adjustments (caused) by the El Nino phenomenon," Fujimori said in a speech outlining his government's anti-poverty strategy.
There are signs the El Nino weather system, which occurs every two to seven years, is starting to form, but its strength will not be known until August, according to meteorologists.

El Nino, which can also affect crops and homes in the southern tier of the United States, northeastern Brazil, southeastern Africa and the west Pacific, causes droughts in the south of Peru and heavy rainfalls in the country's north.

The system's strength can vary dramatically. In the late 1980s, El Nino formed but was barely noticed in Peru, while in 1983, its widespread damage caused the economy to contract more than 12 percent.

If Peru experiences an El Nino this year, the effects would last about 18 months and likely be strongest from December to March, according to the Agriculture Ministry. Cotton, sugar, potato and fruit crops would suffer most among land products.

Fishing unions have also warned the climatic changes could drive fish away from Peru's waters, ruining small businesses in the industry. Fishing is Peru's second largest production sector after mining.
Fujimori added that Peru's current growth -- 2.8 percent last year, and projected at five percent this year -- was accompanied by a rise in international reserves.

"Before, there was growth, from the macroeconomic point of view, but at the cost of reserves," he said. "Now, by contrast, and as a rarety in our economic history, we have at the same time economic growth and rising international reserves."
Peru's reserves currently stand at $9.786 billion.
